note: RBC Royal Bank only: CIBC Caribbean's card schedules for the Bahamas refused the request (403) on the host that serves them, and Republic Bank's weren't reached in this pass. RBC Royal Bank's page of personal credit cards for the Bahamas (read 30 October 2026), read in full: every card it offers individuals (6; the business cards, and the RBC Rewards Visa Platinum Black, offered only to Private Banking clients, a condition the game doesn't check, aren't written), each with its annual fee for the first card, in US dollars where the card is, its purchase rate a year and its cash advance rate a year. The page states no minimum payment, grace period, late fee or foreign transaction fee. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Scotiabank Bahamas, one of the country's largest banks, whose credit card rates and fees page (in effect from 1 January 2022, fees including VAT) was read in full: its personal Mastercards (Scotiabank, Gold, AERO Platinum), Visas (Classic, Gold, AAdvantage) and The Platinum Card American Express, in Bahamian dollars, each with its annual purchase rate (19.00% to 21.00%, 16.00% to 19.00% on the American Express), written at its top with its bottom as the range's lowest, its annual membership fee, its late payment and over-limit charges, a cash advance fee of 3.37%, at least $3.37, its returned cheque charge, a minimum payment of 3%, at least $25 (the American Express's isn't shown), an interest-free period of at least 21 days on purchases paid in full (written as 21) and the rate after a missed minimum payment, up to 21.00%, written as the penalty rate. The business cards and ScotiaLine aren't written; the foreign currency mark-up is 'determined by the Bank from time to time', no figure, so none is written. Tried and not used: Republic Bank's Bahamas site didn't answer. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) also added CIBC Caribbean, one of the region's largest banks, whose Bahamas schedule of charges for cards (effective march 2023, last updated july 2026) its site now serves (an earlier pass found it refused or not linked): read in full, its personal credit cards (9), each with its annual fee for the primary card (none where the schedule gives 0.00 or Free; waived for the first year where the schedule says so), its yearly purchase rate, its cash advance rate and fee, its late payment, over-limit and returned cheque fees, the minimum payment where the schedule gives one, and its late payment rate as the penalty rate, as the earlier CIBC files do. Its business, corporate, commercial and Bizline cards aren't written, nor the replacement, statement, rush card, emergency payment and auto-payment charges, which a holder meets only by asking or by an auto-payment; the UWI cards are for the University of the West Indies' students, faculty and alumni, a condition the game doesn't check. It states no grace period or foreign transaction fee. The Bahamas schedule gives each charge before and with VAT at 10%; the charges with VAT are written; the cash advance fee is 3.30% plus 5.50 dollars with VAT.
